title: Electrochemical batteries and capacity versus power — concept

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: A step that requests more than available energy is invalid. Automatically changing output without explicitly recording curtailed discharge invents a delivered service that was never supplied.
content.text: A useful elementary battery model tracks stored energy in kWh, charge input and delivered discharge power. With fixed one-way efficiencies, stored energy increases by η_charge P_charge Δt and decreases by P_discharge Δt/η_discharge. The difference appears as loss and heat under a chosen accounting boundary. A round trip through the battery returns less electrical energy than supplied unless idealized efficiencies equal one. This says nothing about Coulombic efficiency, calendar aging, nonlinear voltage, cell mismatch or safe charge acceptance. A physically accountable model rejects a step that exceeds capacity rather than silently clipping storage and hiding the excess energy.

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: Do not infer water splitting is over-unity because a fuel cell later returns electricity. Hydrogen storage and gas-handling design require accredited safety practice, absent here.
content.text: Hydrogen is an energy carrier produced from other primary energy sources. Electrolysis uses electrical work to split water, while fuel cells can convert chemical reaction free energy into electrical work. Hydrogen production efficiency must specify lower or higher heating value, water conditions and whether heat inputs are included. Storage and transport require compression, liquefaction or other engineering approaches that consume energy and introduce losses. A hydrogen production pathway can be useful for specific industrial feedstocks or storage use cases, but hydrogen conversion is not a net energy source: the energy delivered from a complete production-storage-conversion chain cannot exceed all energy entering its boundary.

title: Hydrogen and electrochemical conversion pathways — concept

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: Never interpret mechanical storage formulas as instructions to construct high-speed rotors or pressurized vessels. Safe containment, fatigue and fault analysis are specialized fields.
content.text: Electricity can be stored indirectly as gravitational potential, kinetic energy, compressed fluid, phase-change heat or chemical energy. Each mechanism has a different energy density, response time, efficiency, site requirement and durability. Pumped hydro returns water downhill after using electricity to pump it upward, with a round-trip loss. Flywheel energy grows with the square of angular speed, but mechanical stress and containment impose limits. Sensible thermal storage uses heat capacity; phase-change storage adds latent heat at appropriate temperatures. Compressed-air storage interacts with thermodynamics of compression and expansion, so a pressure-only calculation is inadequate. Selecting a technology requires a service definition: seconds of fast response, days of shifting, industrial process heat or seasonal energy supply.

title: Thermal, gravitational, mechanical, and pumped storage — concept

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: A reported CF above one signals inconsistent rated capacity, measurement scope, time interval or data, rather than a breakthrough in energy conversion.
content.text: Power capacity states an instantaneous or sustained rate, while energy capacity states how much service can be delivered over time. A 100 kW generator at 50% capacity factor produces half the energy it would produce at continuous full rating over the defined interval, but capacity factor does not equal thermodynamic efficiency. A battery rated at 100 kW and 100 kWh has a nominal one-hour duration at rated power under ideal conversion, yet usable duration depends on efficiency, allowable discharge and temperature. Capacity factors for intermittent sources must be computed over actual hourly generation, not from one favorable period. Outages, dispatch restrictions and curtailment are distinct contributors to lower output.

title: Power rating, energy capacity, and capacity factor — concept

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: Do not claim a functioning or safe microgrid from an energy-only simulation. A grid needs protection, frequency regulation, grounding and synchronized power-electronic controls.
content.text: A small isolated electrical system must provide sufficient instantaneous power while respecting storage power and energy constraints. A dispatch model consumes timeseries of renewable generation and load, routes surplus into charging where available, and records curtailed generation or imported energy separately. During deficits it discharges storage within limits, then records unmet demand or required grid imports. A daily kWh balance alone cannot guarantee power adequacy at a specific time. Storage dispatch may require forecast uncertainty, reserve policies and reactive power support that a scalar energy model does not provide. A valid ledger must distinguish load actually served from demand requested and must not silently create energy by clipping battery state.

title: Distributed generation, storage dispatch, and unmet load — concept

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: Do not equate annual net-zero energy with continuous reliability or zero environmental impact. The problem is temporal and spatial matching.
content.text: Wind and solar output vary with weather, time and geographic conditions. An average capacity factor cannot reveal whether generation meets load at the right hours. Time correlation between supply and demand, storage duration, interconnection limits and reserve requirements determine reliability. Curtailment means available renewable output is not used because of grid constraints, market signals or equipment conditions; it is not evidence the sunlight or wind contained no energy. A strong analytical library preserves time-series provenance, sampling rate, missing intervals, calendar/time zones, asset rating and measurement uncertainty. Aggregating all hours into one annual energy total can conceal damaging outages.

limitations: A lower LCOE does not automatically mean lower total system cost. Firm capacity, grid reinforcement, reliability and external impacts are outside this simple formula.
content.text: Levelized cost of energy compares discounted lifecycle cost to discounted energy output under a specified project model. It can be useful for alternatives but does not by itself value when electricity is available, how reliably it meets peak demand, local grid constraints or the external impacts of a project. Capital cost, financing, capacity factor, fuel, maintenance, decommissioning, salvage and policy can change results. Real and nominal discount rates must not be mixed with inflation assumptions. A single cost figure cannot represent affordability for every community or determine technology desirability without service and risk analysis.

title: Energy economics, discounted cost, and LCOE — concept

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: No Bitwork energy-saving advantage can be established from a frequency-only synthetic benchmark or from token counts without actual hardware measurements at controlled task quality.
content.text: Computers consume electricity and dissipate heat while performing information processing. The energy used per operation depends on architecture, memory access, switching activity, voltage, clock rate, data movement, cooling and utilization. A count of model tokens, bit operations or agent steps is not by itself joules consumed. Dynamic CMOS power is approximately proportional to switching capacitance, voltage squared and frequency, subject to technology and workload. Memory bandwidth and cooling can dominate arithmetic energy. Energy efficiency comparisons require equal quality targets, measured power over a full interval and consideration of idle baseline. A routing system that reduces apparent model calls may still increase total energy by performing more memory retrieval or verification.

title: Energy in computation and physical information processing — concept

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: A numerical result with many decimal places does not prove high physical accuracy. Calibration and timing traceability determine the defensible significant figures.
content.text: A scientific energy measurement begins by defining the measurand: electrical energy delivered to a load, chemical energy content of fuel, net heat transfer, or whole-facility electricity. Instruments have calibration uncertainty, resolution, drift, bandwidth, phase error and sampling limits. Measuring voltage and current separately does not always recover instantaneous real power, particularly with phase shift or distorted waveforms; a proper power analyzer integrates their product with synchronized sampling. Measurement uncertainties can be correlated, making simple independent-root-sum-of-squares formulas inadequate. A reconstructible result preserves device, calibration record, measurement interval, reference conditions and uncertainty propagation.

title: Energy measurements, uncertainty, and calibration — concept

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: A device efficiency greater than 100% is suspicious only after its precise definition is identified. Claims of net energy creation remain inconsistent with conservation unless unreported inputs or boundaries resolve the discrepancy.
content.text: Energy conversion efficiency, thermodynamic exergetic efficiency, round-trip storage efficiency and generator capacity factor answer different questions. An electric motor can have high conversion efficiency while running only a few hours; its capacity utilization is then low. A heat pump can have COP greater than one while obeying the first and second laws. A thermal engine is bounded by the temperature of its heat source and sink. A perfect first-law balance can still have enormous exergy destruction through mixing or friction. A robust comparison must preserve each metric's numerator, denominator, source boundary, time interval and quality of output.

content.text: Energy technologies have impacts across materials extraction, fabrication, construction, operation, fuel supply, maintenance and end of life. Direct plant-stack emissions are not the same as lifecycle greenhouse-gas intensity. A battery or solar panel may have zero direct combustion emissions during operation but embodied manufacturing impacts, land/water demand and recycling constraints. Assessments must state functional unit such as grams CO2-equivalent per delivered kWh, system boundary, grid mix, recycling allocation and time horizon. Numeric environmental comparisons should come from harmonized datasets, not invented generic constants. Economic and climate objectives can conflict with local ecological or social constraints.

title: Lifecycle impacts, carbon accounting, and resource constraints — concept

applicability: Offline energy physics education and source-qualified interpretation
assumptions: Declared physical model, SI units and scoped boundary required
limitations: Do not energize emergency electrical equipment or attempt grid islanding from this manual. Protective coordination, certification and qualified engineering are essential.
content.text: Power resilience means preserving essential services despite disruptions. A robust microgrid must identify critical loads, generator and storage operating constraints, fault detection, protection, grid-forming controls, communications, fuel supplies and trained operators. The sequence of safe islanding and reconnection is specific to equipment and utility interconnection rules. A simplified energy budget can estimate whether a hospital's nominal battery stores enough kWh, but cannot guarantee safe operation under high inrush currents, reactive loads, faults or equipment failure. Recovery priorities also depend on human needs, not just objective functions. A survival atlas should teach the distinction between energy planning and legally authorized electrical operations.

content.text: Preserving energy knowledge for future generations requires more than an encyclopedia of device names. The library should make it possible to trace a physical service—light, heating, refrigeration, pumping or communications—from energy resource to useful demand through conversion and control. A future reader needs original principles, material properties with source and temperature, calibrated measurement practices, construction standards and safety limitations. It is important to preserve what is not included: this research version cannot safely instruct a nonexpert to build a high-voltage substation, pressure plant or nuclear reactor. Rebuilding technical civilization demands trained people, supply chains and verified standards as well as equations.
